stem: The expanded RPR matrix prints −cosθ3 in row2,column3; multiplying its displayed factors requires which expression?
assumptions: Derive from the consistent factor matrices; the expanded row2,column3 has a source typo.

citations.locator: Lecture7, physical PDF page261, printed slide19; relevant text, table or displayed equation/figure
citations.evidenceText: Factor product displays Rz(θ1), a second transform with Rx(90°) and translation(0,−d2,0), then Rz(θ3) with z offsetL2. Expanded row2,column3 prints−cθ3, whereas multiplying the factors gives−cθ1.

stem: In the differential-drive slide, how do the text definitions of r and 2d relate to the sketch?

options.text: r is turn radius;2d is wheel circumference
r is axle length;2d is heading angle
r is each wheel radius;2d is the separation between wheel centers
r is wheel diameter;2d is distance from axle midpoint to one wheel

citations.locator: Lecture 7, physical PDF page 262, printed slide 20: geometry definitions at left and differential-drive sketch at upper right
citations.evidenceText: The text defines wheel radius r and wheel separation 2d. The sketch shows one d segment between the axle midpoint and one wheel, plus heading φ and position (x,y). It does not label r or the full 2d distance.

stem: The table labels v_r=−v_l as clockwise; which qualification is necessary under the displayed equations?

options.text: It always produces straight backward motion
Its yaw rate is always zero because the average speed is zero
It is clockwise when v_r<0, counterclockwise when v_r>0, and at rest when both wheel speeds are zero
It is always clockwise, even when v_r>0

assumptions: The source’s unconditional clockwise label is incomplete; counterclockwise yaw is positive.

citations.locator: Lecture7, physical PDF page263, printed slide21; relevant text, table or displayed equation/figure
citations.evidenceText: Motion table: v_r=v_l straight; v_r>v_l left; v_r<v_l right; v_r=−v_l labeled clockwise. The last label omits the sign of v_r.
